Text_Reference: 'Abstract': 'We developed ‘ultimate DISCO’ (uDISCO) clearing to overcome these limitations in volumetric imaging.'
'Main section': 'Here, we developed uDISCO, a method that revealed and preserved the signal of endogenous fluorescence over months while retaining the advantageous size reduction.'

General_Description.Text: uDISCO is a tissue-clearing method that preserves fluorescent proteins over months and renders intact organs and rodent bodies transparent while reducing their size up to 65%. It is compatible with various labeling methods and archival human tissue, and it can be used in various biomedical applications to study the organization of large organ systems throughout entire organisms. uDISCO achieves whole-body clearing and imaging due to sample-size reduction and preservation of fluorescent proteins, allowing subcellular imaging of 2× to 3× larger volumes in a single scan.
Text_Reference: 'Abstract': 'uDISCO preserves fluorescent proteins over months and renders intact organs and rodent bodies transparent while reducing their size up to 65%... uDISCO is compatible with diverse labeling methods and archival human tissue, and it can readily be used in various biomedical applications to study organization of large organ systems throughout entire organisms.'
'Main section': 'uDISCO allows subcellular imaging of 2× to 3× larger volumes in a single scan and avoids or reduces artifacts of physical sectioning and mosaic imaging.'
'Discussion': 'uDISCO achieved whole-body clearing and imaging because of sample-size reduction and preservation of fluorescent proteins.'

Tissue_Types.Text2: uDISCO effectively cleared internal organs and hard tissues, including calcified bones, without any additional treatment, such as decalcification with EDTA.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section: 'uDISCO effectively cleared internal organs...without any additional treatment, such as decalcification with EDTA.'

Tissue_Types.Text5: uDISCO successfully cleared whole rats, achieving uniform clearing and over 60% tissue shrinkage of the intact central nervous system.
Text5_Reference: RESULTS section: 'uDISCO successfully cleared whole rats...achieving uniform clearing and over 60% tissue shrinkage of the intact central nervous system.'

Tissue_Types.Text16: uDISCO is applicable to formalin-fixed human clinical tissue samples, causing volume shrinkage of approximately 46-52%, and is compatible with antibody labeling without requiring extra antigen retrieval steps.
Text16_Reference: Results Section: 'To determine whether uDISCO could be applied to such specimens, we immunostained 1-mm-thick human samples (archived for either 1 month or 14 months) for GFAP and TO-PRO-3 or Iba1 and TO-PRO-3.'
'We measured shrinkage of 52% and 46% in samples stored for 1 month or 14 months, respectively (Fig. 6m,n).'
'Importantly, the combination of uDISCO and deep-tissue antibody labeling did not require additional antigen retrieval steps.'

human: 1mm clinical cortical tissue samples of human brains

Time_Consumption.Text1: The whole body of an adult Thy1–GFP-M mouse can be cleared within 3–4 days using uDISCO.
Text1_Reference: Articles section: 'We cleared the whole body of an adult Thy1–GFP-M mouse within 3–4 d (Fig. 2a,b; 3-month-old mouse; the skin was removed before clearing).'

Tissue_Deformation.Text1: In brain tissue, uDISCO-induced shrinkage is isotropic and homogenous, with structures and various cell types shrinking uniformly while preserving their morphology. However, this isotropic shrinkage has yet to be confirmed for other tissues like muscle or fat.
Text1_Reference: Results Section: 'To test whether the shrinkage was isotropic, we compared images before and after clearing. We found that brain tissues such as the cortex and hippocampal layers shrank homogenously, ∼30% in each dimension at macroscopic scale (Supplementary Fig. 12).'

'...the shrinkage of different cell types (neurons, glia, etc.) and vasculature in the same brain region was homogenous in all dimensions... individual cell and vascular morphologies were preserved in brain tissue after uDISCO clearing'

Discussion Section: 'uDISCO did not alter the structural integrity of the brain either at macroscopic...or microscopic scales... However, isotropic shrinkage remains to be confirmed for other tissues such as muscle or fat'

Tissue_Deformation.Text2: uDISCO typically reduces tissue volume. For example, it shrank whole mice by ~42%, adult mouse brains by up to 55%, and intact adult rats to 40% of their original volume.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section: '...whole-body clearing by uDISCO reduced the volume of mice (~42%)...'
RESULTS section: '...uDISCO reduced the size of adult mouse brains up to 55%...'
Figure Legend: 'intact 4-week-old rats':'40% of original volume'

Application.Text1: Using uDISCO, entire bodies of adult rodents can be imaged to determine long-distance neuronal and vascular projections, as well as the spatial distribution of stem cell transplants at single-cell resolution.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'Using uDISCO, we imaged entire bodies of adult rodents to determine long-distance neuronal and vascular projections and spatial information on stem cell transplants...at single-cell resolution.'

Application.Text2: uDISCO enables unbiased, whole-body screening and analysis of transplanted cells (including stem cells) at single-cell resolution, allowing for the study of their density and distribution.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section: 'Overall, our data demonstrate that uDISCO whole-body clearing can be used to study density and distribution of fluorescently labeled transplanted cells throughout the entire host body at single-cell resolution.'

RESULTS section, 'uDISCO allows interrogation of BMSCs in the entire mouse': 'We used uDISCO whole-body clearing for an unbiased screen of transplanted syngeneic mouse BMSCs in the entire body at single-cell resolution.'

Application.Text3: uDISCO, combined with light-sheet microscopy, allows for tracing individual axons over several centimeters in the entire adult mouse CNS and achieves dendritic spine resolution, a first for an organic-solvent-based clearing method in an intact brain.
Text3_Reference: Results Section,'uDISCO allows tracing of the intact central nervous system': '...we used uDISCO to trace neuronal structures from head to toe in the entire CNS (brain and spinal cord) of 3- to 5-month-old Thy1–GFP-M adult mice. We could trace individual axons in the intact CNS over several centimeters in these scans.'

'For the first time for an organic-solvent-based clearing method in intact adult mouse brain, uDISCO achieved dendritic-spine resolution using light-sheet microscopy (Fig. 4g and Supplementary Video 8).'

Application.Text4: uDISCO is compatible with alternative labeling methods such as adeno-associated virus (AAV) tracing and deep-tissue immunostaining.
Text4_Reference: RESULTS section, 'uDISCO is compatible with virus labeling and immunostaining': 'Most animal models used in the laboratory... do not express fluorescent proteins. Hence, we sought to test alternative methods to label tissues for uDISCO.'

RESULTS section, 'uDISCO is compatible with virus labeling and immunostaining': 'To test these methods with uDISCO, we cut 1-mm-thick tissue sections of mouse brains and labeled them with antibodies...'

Application.Text5: When applied to the central nervous system, uDISCO combined with AAV tracing allows for the visualization of specific structures, such as the pyramidal decussation, and the detection of axon bundles several centimeters long.
Text5_Reference: Results Section: 'The pyramidal decussation of descending motor axons was clearly visible (Fig. 6c). We detected both bundles of axons as well as individual axons in the brain and spinal cord over several centimeters (Fig. 6d–f).'

Application.Text6: From an application perspective, uDISCO can successfully clear and enable imaging of human tissue samples that have been stored in formalin for over a year, while preserving signals from antibody staining.
Text6_Reference: Results Section: 'uDISCO allowed successful clearing, signal preservation, and imaging of human tissues stored in formalin more than a year (Fig. 6o–r and Supplementary Fig. 25), although the image quality was better for shorter storage periods (Supplementary Fig. 25i).'

Note.text: uDISCO provides an advantage for imaging large volumes because it both preserves fluorescent protein signals and substantially reduces tissue size.
Text_reference: Results section, 'uDISCO preserves endogenous signal and reduces volume by 65%' :'This size reduction, together with uDISCO's preservation of fluorescent proteins, resulted in a substantial advantage for imaging larger volumes compared with other tissue-clearing methods. '

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: uDISCO demonstrates broad compatibility with various fluorescence labeling methods, including genetically encoded proteins, viral tracers, antibody stains, and synthetic fluorescent dyes.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'uDISCO reveals fluorescence notably better and maintains it several weeks longer within Thy1–GFP-M mouse brains...'
Results Section: '...we sought to test alternative methods to label tissues for uDISCO. To this end, we used adeno-associated virus (AVV) tracing...'
Results Section: '...labeled them with antibodies against glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)...'
Results Section: '...observe the details of Texas Red–dextran-labeled vasculature...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: The method is compatible with endogenous signals like GFP, revealing fluorescence notably better than methods such as 3DISCO or ScaleS.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'uDISCO preserves endogenous signal and reduces volume by 65%': 'uDISCO reveals fluorescence notably better and maintains it several weeks longer within Thy1–GFP-M mouse brains...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text3: uDISCO is compatible with viral tracing; fluorescence from AAV-delivered proteins was detectable throughout the brain and intact spinal cord.
Text3_Reference: Results Section: 'To this end, we used adeno-associated virus (AVV) tracing to label neurons in the CNS of mice.'
'Fluorescence expression of the virally delivered proteins was detectable in the brain and throughout the intact spinal cord...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text4: The method is compatible with deep-tissue antibody labeling, successfully visualizing signals from antibodies like anti-GFAP and anti-Iba1 in thick tissue sections.
Text4_Reference: Results Section: '...the signals from GFAP (astrocytes), Iba1 (microglia and macrophages)... were visible throughout the tissue, indicating compatibility of uDISCO with deep-tissue labeling...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text5: It is also compatible with synthetic fluorescent dyes, for example, allowing visualization of vasculature labeled with Texas Red–dextran in an intact rat.
Text5_Reference: Results Section: 'We could observe the details of Texas Red–dextran-labeled vasculature in the brain, brainstem, and limbs using a standard fluorescence stereomicroscope in the intact 4-week-old rats (Fig. 3c–f). '

Preservation_Stability.Text1: uDISCO preserves fluorescent signals for an extended period, allowing fine structures in cleared tissue to be detected for weeks to months. This stability is notably better and lasts several weeks longer compared to methods like 3DISCO and ScaleS.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'uDISCO reveals fluorescence notably better and maintains it several weeks longer within Thy1–GFP-M mouse brains...'
RESULTS section: 'With the resulting protocol, the fine structures of labeled neurons in the lipid-dense brain and spinal cord can be detected over weeks to months.'

Preservation_Stability.Text2: The signal intensity, after an initial decrease within the first few weeks, stabilizes after approximately one month. At all time points, the fluorescence level remains higher than that of 3DISCO-treated samples.
Text2_Reference: Supplementary Figure 4: 'We observed some decrease in signal level within the first few weeks, which got stabilized after about a month. At all-time points, the level of fluorescence after uDISCO was higher compared with the level of fluorescence after 3DISCO.'
